name: Second Act
tagline: Design a retirement you'll actually enjoy
about: Second Act helps new and soon-to-be retirees build a weekly rhythm, find hobbies and purpose, plan the trips and projects on the list, and handle the identity shift that nobody warns you about.
persona: You are a warm retirement-transition coach: practical, curious, allergic to clichés, focused on structure, connection and meaning rather than money.

onboarding.title: Your time, your terms
onboarding.subtitle: Tell us where you are in the transition and what lights you up.
bullets: A weekly rhythm that fits you
Hobbies and purpose matched to you

profile.label: Things you've always enjoyed
profile.placeholder: gardening, crosswords, old cars, church choir

tools.title: Design my week
tools.subtitle: Structure without a boss

inputs.label: I want a week that is

tools.prompt: Design a weekly rhythm for the profile, style: {style}, around fixed commitments: {fixed}. A table (Day | Morning | Afternoon | Evening) with anchors rather than minute-by-minute schedules, bullets on the 3 anchors that matter most (movement, people, purpose), and a callout on protecting unstructured time.

tools.title: Find a new hobby
tools.subtitle: Matched to hands, budget and energy
tools.prompt: Suggest 5 {kind} hobbies for the profile with a start budget of {budget}: cards (meta = cost to start · solo or social · energy needed), each with why it suits the profile's interests. Then steps to try the best-fit one in the next 7 days, and bullets of where to find local groups or beginner classes (types of venues, not specific addresses).

tools.title: Purpose after work
tools.subtitle: Volunteering, mentoring, projects

inputs.label: What you were good at
inputs.placeholder: 35 years in nursing; organising people; fixing things

tools.prompt: From: {skills} — propose 4 ways to contribute as cards (meta = hours per week · commitment length), covering one volunteering role, one mentoring or teaching idea, one community project and one light paid option. Then a kv (First call to make | What to say | What to ask), and a quote with a one-sentence 'what I do now' answer for parties.

tools.title: Plan a big one
tools.subtitle: Trip, project or milestone
tools.prompt: Turn '{dream}' by {when} into a plan for the profile's energy level: steps in order with rough dates working back from {when}, a table (Item | Estimated cost | Book by), a checklist of health, mobility and insurance preparation, and a callout on the one thing people regret not booking early.

tools.title: Who am I now?
tools.subtitle: The shift nobody warns you about

inputs.label: How it's going
inputs.placeholder: I feel useless on Monday mornings; my partner is fed up with me being underfoot

tools.prompt: Respond to: {feeling}. A text section that names the transition honestly and normalises it, bullets of 4 small experiments to try this week, a quote with a script for a conversation with a partner or friend about the change, and a callout on signs that low mood has become more than adjustment and it's worth talking to a GP.

disclaimer: Second Act offers lifestyle ideas, not financial, medical or mental-health advice; talk to a professional for those.
